title: Vedic Atlas
scope: Supplied input files only; semantic annotations are selective.

nodes.title: Vedic literature · supplied collection
nodes.summary: An evidence-linked map of the supplied Veda, Upanishad, Purana, and practical-guide PDFs. Explore works, hymns, narratives, shared concepts, source editions, and every PDF page.

nodes.title: Four Vedic traditions
nodes.summary: Hymns, ritual formulas, chants, and selected translations. The files have different scopes and sometimes overlap.

nodes.title: 108 Upanishads
nodes.summary: The supplied Muktika-ordered collection, with the ten modern commentaries kept distinct from translations.

nodes.title: 18 named Puranas
nodes.summary: Narrative, devotional, cosmological, ritual, and pilgrimage material. Many supplied files are retellings or partial volumes.

nodes.title: Practical guides
nodes.summary: The supplied Ayurveda, yoga, and Vastu guides, organized separately from the scriptural texts.

nodes.title: Ideas & recurring figures
nodes.summary: Navigation through shared names and themes. Textual mentions and editorial comparisons do not establish historical borrowing or identical doctrine.

nodes.title: Rigveda
nodes.summary: Ten books of hymns in the supplied English translation. All 1,028 observed HYMN headings are indexed; hymn names and occasional misspellings follow this file. A metrical glossary follows the hymns.

nodes.title: Samaveda
nodes.summary: Songs arranged for ritual chanting. The supplied Griffith preface describes verses drawn mainly from the Rigveda and rearranged for ritual. The 460 song groups below use the explicit hierarchy in the indexed draft compilation; a separate Stevenson translation is also supplied.

nodes.title: Yajurveda
nodes.summary: Two distinct supplied presentations: the 40-chapter Tulsi Ram translation, and Keith’s numbered Taittiriya passages in the Four Vedas compilation. Their section numbering and interpretive traditions are preserved separately.

nodes.title: Atharvaveda
nodes.summary: Whitney/Lanman volume I supplies books I–VII with critical commentary, 433 hymns under its Berlin numbering. Bloomfield’s supplied anthology adds selections from later books and explicitly says it covers about one third of the entire material.

nodes.title: Brahma Upanishad
nodes.summary: Pippalada teaches Saunaka about the inner Brahman, life-breath and the sacred thread understood as knowledge.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Kaivalya Upanishad
nodes.summary: Brahma teaches Asvalayana that faith, devotion, meditation and renunciation lead to the highest knowledge.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Jabala Upanishad
nodes.summary: Yajnavalkya explains Avimukta and renunciation; treats the conditions and conduct of the wandering ascetic.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Svetasvatara Upanishad
nodes.summary: Investigates the cause of existence, the Lord, the self, nature and the discipline through which reality is known.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Hamsa Upanishad
nodes.summary: Sanatkumara teaches Gautama the Hamsa discipline, breath-linked contemplation and inner sound.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Aruni Upanishad
nodes.summary: Brahma instructs Aruni on abandoning ritual possessions and worldly ties for the knowledge of Brahman.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Garbha Upanishad
nodes.summary: Presents a traditional account of embryonic development, bodily elements and the body interpreted as sacrifice.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Narayana Upanishad
nodes.summary: Praises Narayana as the source and identity of all; expounds the eight-syllable Om Namo Narayanaya mantra.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Paramahamsa Upanishad
nodes.summary: Brahma answers Narada about the inward freedom, duties and outward simplicity of the Paramahamsa ascetic.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Amrita Bindu Upanishad
nodes.summary: Explains how desire binds the mind and how the mind freed from sense objects becomes a means of liberation.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Amrita-Nada Upanishad
nodes.summary: Uses the chariot of Om as an image for contemplation and sets out disciplines of yoga and breath.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Atharvasiras Upanishad
nodes.summary: Identifies Rudra with the gods, cosmic regions and Om; explains the one principle through many divine names.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Atharvasikha Upanishad
nodes.summary: Atharva answers sages about meditation on Om and its four aspects, deities and Vedic correspondences.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Maitrayani Upanishad
nodes.summary: King Brihadratha renounces his throne and asks the sage Sakayana for self-knowledge beyond decaying embodiment.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Kaushitaki Brahmana Upanishad
nodes.summary: Contains dialogues about rebirth, life-breath and consciousness, including Indra-Pratardana and Balaki-Ajatasatru.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Brihad Jabala Upanishad
nodes.summary: Busunda questions Kalagni Rudra about sacred ash, Rudraksha and Shaiva observance as a path to liberation.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Nrisimhatapini Upanishad
nodes.summary: Presents Poorva and Uttara Narasimha Tapaniya translations on Narasimha, mantra, Om and the supreme self.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Kalagni Rudra Upanishad
nodes.summary: Kalagnirudra explains the three ash marks of Tripundra and their ritual and contemplative correspondences.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Maitreya Upanishad
nodes.summary: Retells Brihadratha's disenchantment with embodied life and sets out self-knowledge and the renunciant's discipline.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Subala Upanishad
nodes.summary: Describes cosmic emergence and dissolution, the inner self and Narayana as the basis of beings.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Kshurika Upanishad
nodes.summary: Uses a sharp knife of wisdom and inward yoga as imagery for cutting attachment; this version marks verses 2–9 unavailable.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Mantrika Upanishad
nodes.summary: Presents the subtle, imperishable reality through swan imagery and the relation of knowledge, nature and the absolute.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Sarva Sara Upanishad
nodes.summary: Defines bondage, liberation, ignorance, knowledge, consciousness states, sheaths, individual self and the absolute.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Niralamba Upanishad
nodes.summary: Uses a sequence of questions and answers to define Brahman, God, the individual, nature, knowledge and liberation.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Suka Rahasya Upanishad
nodes.summary: Shiva teaches Suka the inner meaning of great Upanishadic sayings, including That Thou Art.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Vajrasuchika Upanishad
nodes.summary: Examines what makes a Brahmana and rejects body, birth and mere social designation as sufficient criteria.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Tejo-Bindu Upanishad
nodes.summary: Teaches meditation on the seed of spiritual light and develops knowledge of the nondual self.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Nada Bindu Upanishad
nodes.summary: Interprets Om as a bird and develops contemplation on inner sound as a means of freeing the mind.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Dhyana-Bindu Upanishad
nodes.summary: Connects seed-syllable, spiritual sound, contemplation and yogic processes with the supreme state beyond sound.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Brahma Vidya Upanishad
nodes.summary: Explains Om through its syllables, their Vedic and divine correspondences, inner location and dissolution.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Yoga Tattva Upanishad
nodes.summary: Vishnu teaches Brahma the relation of yoga and knowledge and describes yogic disciplines leading to liberation.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Atma-Bodha Upanishad
nodes.summary: Contemplates Narayana and Om as inner Brahman and develops assertions of the self's freedom and consciousness.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Narada Parivrajaka Upanishad
nodes.summary: Narada asks Brahma about renunciation; treats eligibility, conduct, classifications and inner knowledge of ascetics.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Trisikhi Brahmana Upanishad
nodes.summary: A Brahmana questions the Sun about body, self and cause; the reply links cosmology, inner faculties and yoga.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Sita Upanishad
nodes.summary: Prajapati explains Sita as primordial nature and divine power, relating her to sound, knowledge and manifestation.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Yoga Chudamani Upanishad
nodes.summary: Teaches breath, Hamsa and yogic ascent; this supplied translation explicitly omits verses 2–29.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Nirvana Upanishad
nodes.summary: Describes the Paramahamsa through inward renunciation and symbolic identifications of the ascetic life.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Mandala Brahmana Upanishad
nodes.summary: The solar Narayana teaches Yajnavalkya eightfold yoga, knowledge and inward contemplation of light.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Dakshinamurti Upanishad
nodes.summary: Sages ask Markandeya about his enduring life and joy; he teaches the secret knowledge and mantra of Dakshinamurti.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Sarabha Upanishad
nodes.summary: Praises Shiva as supreme and narrates Sarabha's subduing of Narasimha within this text's Shaiva presentation.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Skanda Upanishad
nodes.summary: Presents the identity of Shiva and Vishnu and teaches the nonseparation of the individual self and the divine.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Tripadvibhuti Mahanarayana Upanishad
nodes.summary: Presents Narayana as the source of all beings and cosmic forces; expounds Om Namo Narayanaya through eight-syllable mantra and inward realization.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Advaya Taraka Upanishad
nodes.summary: Teaches nondual reality through neti-neti, inner light, Taraka yoga and guidance by a qualified teacher.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Rama Rahasya Upanishad
nodes.summary: Hanuman explains Rama's sacred formulae, their ritual arrangements and their liberating significance.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Rama Tapaniya Upanishad
nodes.summary: Contains Poorva and Uttara parts on Rama, Sita, devotional visualization and the saving Rama mantra.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Vasudeva Upanishad
nodes.summary: Vasudeva teaches Narada the rules and significance of the upward Vaishnava forehead mark.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Mudgala Upanishad
nodes.summary: Interprets the Purusha Sukta in terms of Vishnu's pervasion, the fourfold Purusha and liberation.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Sandilya Upanishad
nodes.summary: Atharvan answers Sandilya on eightfold yoga, including ethical disciplines, postures, breath and meditation.
nodes.method: Body heading and end colophon; summary of supplied translation.

nodes.title: Paingala Upanishad
nodes.summary: Yajnavalkya teaches Paingala about secondless Brahman, creation, inner faculties and liberating knowledge.

notes.title: Scope of completeness
notes.text: All 30 supplied PDFs and all 7,984 physical PDF pages are represented. All 108 catalogued Upanishads and the machine-indexed Vedic and Purana headings are navigable. Curated narrative summaries and semantic links are selective, not an exhaustive scholarly annotation of every embedded story or verse.

notes.title: How to read a connection
notes.text: Contains means an organizational parent. Source points to a PDF page. Mentions means a literal term match, including front matter or modern commentary where present. Theme and comparison links are editorial. Traditional affiliation follows the supplied compilation; none of these relations proves historical derivation.

notes.title: Page references
notes.text: Every reference uses one-based PDF page numbers, not printed page or verse numbers. A section and its following commentary can begin or end on the same physical page.

notes.title: Text recognition
notes.text: Matsya, Brahmanda, and the yoga guide required local OCR. OCR can misread names, numbers, accents, and columns. Open the original scan to check any quotation.

notes.title: Vedas
notes.text: Scope is the supplied PDFs, not all recensions, manuscripts, Brahmanas, Aranyakas, Sutras, or all Hindu literature.

notes.title: Vedas
notes.text: Rigveda: all 1,028 observed HYMN headings indexed in 10 books. Machine numbering follows heading order within each book because several Roman numerals are mistyped.

notes.title: Vedas
notes.text: Samaveda: 460 actual song groups from the draft compilation body, plus 51 structural nodes. The source’s inconsistent mantra totals are not treated as established counts. Stevenson’s separate OCR translation remains available through source pages.

notes.title: Vedas
notes.text: Yajurveda: 40 Tulsi Ram chapters indexed. Keith numbered passage headings indexed separately without assuming a one-to-one match to the 40-chapter edition. Some source references are malformed (e.g. iii.6.8 between iii.5.7 and iii.5.9; iv.8.4 between iv.3.3 and iv.3.5; vii.6.16 between vii.5.15 and vii.5.17); labels are retained with source pages.

notes.title: Vedas
notes.text: Atharvaveda: Whitney/Lanman volume I supplies Books I–VII only. Its Berlin numbering has 35,36,31,40,31,142,118 hymns respectively, totaling 433. Book VII includes different parenthesized Bombay numbering; no automatic equivalence is asserted.

notes.title: Vedas
notes.text: Bloomfield anthology introduction (Four Vedas p1313) explicitly calls itself about one third of the entire material. Later-book selections are indexed; this does not make later books complete.

notes.title: Vedas
notes.text: the-4-vedas-in-1 is Issue 1, Draft 2 and has many literal “Sukta text here” placeholders in the Atharva portion. These placeholders are excluded as hymn content. Its editorial merger of recensions and speculative totals are not endorsed.

notes.title: Vedas
notes.text: 472 Sama–Rig reading links were generated from exact 12-word English matches, with evidence on both sides. These links show translation wording overlap, not a verified philological stemma or complete identity.

notes.title: Vedas
notes.text: The first ten Rigveda key-summary examples and other curated summaries are editorial reading aids grounded in their cited passages. Other heading-only summaries do not claim a full interpretive analysis of each hymn.

notes.title: Upanishads
notes.text: All 108 numbered Muktika catalog entries were found in the supplied compilation. Catalog numbers are navigation identifiers, not composition dates.

notes.title: Upanishads
notes.text: PDF page numbers are one-based physical pages, not printed page numbers. Ten modern commentaries sometimes begin on the same PDF page as the end of the translation; both nodes therefore legitimately share a boundary page.

notes.title: Upanishads
notes.text: The Mandukya translation proper occupies pages 181–182; Gaudapada’s separately titled Karika occupies pages 182–193, followed by Nirmalananda Giri’s modern commentary on pages 193–197.

notes.title: Upanishads
notes.text: Nrisimhatapini is catalog item 27; the compilation supplies separate Poorva and Uttara translations and explicitly notes the alternate counting. They are child sections, not two extra entries in the 108.

notes.title: Upanishads
notes.text: Rama Tapaniya also contains Poorva and Uttara sections; both remain children of the one catalog entry.

notes.title: Upanishads
notes.text: Kshurika explicitly marks verses 2–9 unavailable; Yoga Chudamani marks verses 2–29 unavailable. These gaps belong to the supplied edition and are not silently filled.

notes.title: Upanishads
notes.text: Avyakta as supplied presents transliterated Nasadiya, Hiranyagarbha and Purusha Suktas with a compiler-style introduction; it is indexed as supplied, without asserting textual-critical completeness.

notes.title: Upanishads
notes.text: All summaries and episodes refer to the supplied translations. Extra anecdotes and interpretations inside modern commentaries are not labeled as original Upanishadic stories.

notes.title: Upanishads
notes.text: Vedic affiliations, where recorded, follow the compilation’s traditional colophons and Muktika grouping; affiliation is not proof that the supplied independent Samhita PDF contains that Upanishad.

notes.title: Upanishads
notes.text: Thematic comparisons are editorial navigation links. They do not establish chronology, textual derivation or uniform doctrine. Sectarian differences are retained.

notes.title: Upanishads
notes.text: Tags record terms attested in the primary translation, including recurring invocations; they are discovery aids rather than proof of an episode-level or doctrinal relationship. Curated edges carry their own passage evidence.

notes.title: Puranas
notes.text: The supplied library contains 20 Purana PDFs representing 18 named Purana works. Shiva and Vishnu are each split over two overlapping files.

notes.title: Puranas
notes.text: Most text-readable Purana PDFs are short English overviews or retellings with modern editorial comments. A file bearing a Purana name is not evidence that the whole Sanskrit work is present.

notes.title: Puranas
notes.text: Skanda is explicitly Part I: Book I, Maheshvarakhanda, Section I, Kedarakhanda, chapters 1–35. PDF page = printed page + 4. Chapter 6 is corrected to PDF 46 (actual printed 42); the contents list incorrectly says 41.

notes.title: Puranas
notes.text: Brahma Vaivarta supplied file: introductory description and numbered narrative body differ in emphasis. Retain supplied identification and avoid certifying canonical completeness.

notes.title: Puranas
notes.text: Narada supplied file begins with Linga Purana carryover on PDF page 1; Narada section 18.1 begins on PDF page 2.

notes.title: Puranas
notes.text: Shiva volume 1 pages 47 and volume 2 page 1 overlap at sections 5.2.126–5.2.129; Vishnu volume 1 page 39 and volume 2 page 1 overlap at section 3.4.4. Keep these witnesses separate, not additional stories.

notes.title: Puranas
notes.text: Bhavishya prediction and historical assertions are the supplied edition’s claims. No external chronology or historical authentication was performed.

notes.title: Puranas
notes.text: Heading extraction gives navigable source units, not verified Sanskrit verse/chapter numbering. Numbering such as 16.10.20 belongs to the supplied retelling.

notes.title: Puranas
notes.text: Section summaries labeled extracted heading with passage opening are shortened source openings; curated readings are explicitly marked. Shared-narrative edges are title-attested comparison links, not historical derivation or proof of theological agreement.

notes.title: Puranas
notes.text: Matsya and Brahmanda initially had no extractable text; OCR-generated headings, if added by the main analysis, must retain their OCR status. Visual title evidence identifies the Matsya scan as Matsya Puranam Part I (1916), rather than a complete Purana.

notes.title: Scanned puranas
notes.text: Matsya supplied scan identifies itself as Volume XVII, Part I, chapters 1–128 (title page PDF3). Its translated body occupies PDF19–380. It is not the complete canonical Matsya Purana.

notes.title: Scanned puranas
notes.text: Matsya Appendix III additionally translates chapters 271–273 (PDF407–428). The remaining appendices are largely modern editorial discussions and genealogical tables, indexed separately from scripture.

notes.title: Scanned puranas
notes.text: Brahmanda supplied scan identifies itself as PART III (PDF6) and Section III continuation. It contains chapters 44–74 (PDF10–248), not the whole Brahmanda Purana.

notes.title: Scanned puranas
notes.text: Both PDFs are image scans. These navigation nodes use locally generated OCR, whose spelling, diacritics and Roman chapter numerals can contain recognition errors. Display titles normalize obvious heading errors; evidence excerpts preserve the OCR wording.

notes.title: Scanned puranas
notes.text: Matsya chapter 13 begins on PDF57 after the chapter12 colophon without a recognizable chapter13 heading in the OCR. The boundary was identified from the following dialogue and chapter13 colophon atPDF61.

notes.title: Scanned puranas
notes.text: Chapter ranges are inclusive navigation spans to the next heading page, so adjoining chapters may legitimately share one PDF page. They are not verse-level critical segmentation.

notes.title: Scanned puranas
